title: Vulkan Tutorial — Overview
excerpt: Why Vulkan exists, the 8-step triangle pipeline, and how the API is structured at a low level.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Base Code
excerpt: The HelloTriangleApplication class structure, explicit Vulkan resource lifecycle, and GLFW window integration that form the base for every subsequent chapter.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Instance
excerpt: Creating a VkInstance — the root Vulkan object — by filling VkApplicationInfo and VkInstanceCreateInfo, querying GLFW extensions, and handling the macOS portability edge case.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Logical Device & Queues
excerpt: Creating a VkDevice from the selected physical device, requesting a graphics queue, and understanding why vkDestroyDevice must be the first cleanup call.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Physical Devices & Queue Families
excerpt: Enumerating GPUs with vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices, evaluating suitability, and finding a queue family that supports graphics commands using std::optional for clean index tracking.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Validation Layers
excerpt: Adding VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation, wiring up the debug messenger with proxy functions, and using the pNext chain to catch errors inside vkCreateInstance itself.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Window Surface
excerpt: Creating a VkSurfaceKHR via glfwCreateWindowSurface, adding a present queue family to QueueFamilyIndices, and using std::set to deduplicate queue creation when graphics and present share the same family index.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Swap Chain
excerpt: Negotiating surface format, present mode, and swap extent; setting imageCount, sharing mode, compositeAlpha, and clipped; then retrieving VkImage handles with vkGetSwapchainImagesKHR.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Image Views
excerpt: Wrapping each swap chain VkImage in a VkImageView — configuring viewType, format, component swizzle, and subresourceRange — and understanding why views require explicit cleanup while the images themselves do not.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Graphics Pipeline Introduction
excerpt: The seven pipeline stages in order, which are fixed-function vs programmable, why the geometry shader is avoided in practice, why Vulkan pipelines are immutable, and when the fragment shader can be disabled.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Fixed Functions
excerpt: Every fixed-function pipeline struct: dynamic state, vertex input, input assembly, viewport/scissor, rasterizer gotchas (GPU feature requirements), MSAA efficiency, color blend vs logic op exclusivity, alpha blending formula, and why VkPipelineLayout is mandatory even when empty.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Shader Modules
excerpt: Why Vulkan requires SPIR-V, compiling GLSL with glslc, loading .spv files with ios::binary, wrapping bytecode in VkShaderModule, wiring stages with VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo, and destroying modules immediately after pipeline creation.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Render Passes
excerpt: How VkAttachmentDescription declares load/store ops and image layout transitions, the VkAttachmentReference → fragment shader location linkage, subpass bandwidth optimization, and why createRenderPass() must precede createGraphicsPipeline().

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Graphics Pipeline Conclusion
excerpt: Assembling all four components into VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo, why vkCreateGraphicsPipelines accepts an array, what VkPipelineCache enables across program runs, pipeline derivatives, and render pass compatibility.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Framebuffers
excerpt: How VkFramebuffer binds the abstract attachments declared by a render pass to concrete VkImageView objects, why one framebuffer per swap chain image is required, VkFramebufferCreateInfo fields, and cleanup ordering.

title: Vulkan Tutorial — Command Buffers
excerpt: Command pools and per-buffer reset, primary vs secondary command buffer levels, the begin/render-pass/draw/end recording bracket, why viewport and scissor must be set dynamically, and vkCmdDraw's hardcoded triangle parameters.
